items.title: Storm Postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade, Trump's New Tariffs, Iowa Post-Detonation
items.summary: Powerful storms threaten to disrupt Thanksgiving travel for millions of Americans and have forced the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to be postponed for the first time in its history. The Trump administration is proposing new tariffs on goods from fourteen major trading partners, setting up another potential legal fight over the president’s trade policies. The Army is calling its controlled detonation of unstable explosives in Iowa a success, but some residents are waiting for independent test results before trusting assurances about lead contamination.
items.body: Powerful storms threaten to disrupt Thanksgiving travel for millions of Americans and have forced the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to be postponed for the first time in its history. items.title: German boat dealer suspected of supplying Channel smuggling gangs, BBC finds
items.summary: Nearly a third of crossings in early 2026 allegedly involved boats or engines from the German man's firm.
items.body: A German boat dealer is suspected by European authorities of being a key supplier to migrant smugglers operating in the English Channel, the BBC can reveal. Nearly a third of small-boat crossings in the first four months of this year allegedly involved boats or engines from MaReBoote, a small firm in western Germany, according to files we have seen.

items.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
items.summary: Lenacapavir, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.
items.body: Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.

items.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.summary: Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.
items.body: A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.summary: Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed. Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.
items.body: Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

items.title: ‘I was very aggressive. They threw me out of every school’ … Julie Delpy on acting, anger and predatory directors
items.summary: Thirty years after the roles that made her famous, the star of Three Colours: White and the Before trilogy is busier than ever – as a screenwriter and director. But, she says, a lot of people have tried to keep her down To listen to Julie Delpy talk about her workload is to feel the need for a nap coming on. She is writing six screenplays at the moment that range from dark comedies to thrillers. “I don’t do monoculture,” she says. If her producer hadn’t reined her in, she would be working on five horror film scripts too. The actor, writer and director says she doesn’t sleep well – she can sit at her desk for up to 18 hours, writing “until I run out of steam. I know you could think I’m exaggerating. I’m not. If you look at my computer, you will see how bad it is.” We’re on a video call, Delpy from her home in Los Angeles. She is charming – intense and funny in big black-framed glasses. “I look so weird with this angle on my hair,” she says, of the ceiling light behind her. “Like an angry bald man!”

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album review – even GTA sceptics will warm to this zeitgeisty, star-packed soundtrack
items.summary: (Atlantic) Justice bring some 80s nostalgia but this compilation of new material from music’s A-list – from Dua Lipa to Travis Scott and a host of Latin talent – stays at the cutting edge It can be hard to ascertain why Grand Theft Auto VI is such a phenomenon from merely watching along with it. Equally devoted to the thrill of a violent crime story and a more mundane lifestyle fantasy, the appeal does not always translate to bystanders. Its soundtrack, however, is another story: a compilation of brand new material from some of the biggest pop, rap, rock and country artists on the planet – some of them combined in imaginative pileups of guest features – that can be enjoyed totally separately from the gameplay, if you so wish. Starting from Zero, the opener by Justice – also composers of the game’s original score, released on 11 December – features the unmistakable voice of the Doobie Brothers’ Michael McDonald belting out an 80s-style pop ballad complete with a saxophone outro. This style is synonymous with Grand Theft Auto VI’s setting, a fictionalised version of Florida last seen in 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was beloved for its inclusion of 80s hits.

items.title: Young people are having less sex. What's going on? - video
items.summary: Sex among British adults has slumped in recent decades, with under-45s having half as many monthly encounters as in 1990 and one in three under-25s reporting that they have never had sexual intercourse. To unpick some of the possible reasons behind these declines, Madeleine Finlay hears from science editor and co-host Ian Sample. He tells her why young people might be having sex later, and what could account for the striking rise in women reporting that they don’t want children.

items.title: Contraceptive pill usage in Great Britain fell drastically in last decade, research finds
items.summary: Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception.

items.title: God or glory: why did people go on crusade?
items.summary: In 1095, Pope Urban II made a call to arms that would completely transform the medieval world, setting in motion a wave of crusading zeal that would ripple on for centuries. Promising spiritual reward to those willing to take up the cross and journey east to fight for Jerusalem, his speech resulted in the violent capture of the Holy City and formation of a new world of crusader states.But why did this message resonate so powerfully with the medieval mindset? 2021 — COVID-19 pandemic: The World Health Organization identifies the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.

2019 — A magnitude 6.4 earthquake strikes western Albania leaving at least 52 people dead and over 1,000 injured. This was the world's deadliest earthquake of 2019, and the deadliest to strike the country in 99 years.

2018 — The robotic probe Insight lands on Elysium Planitia, Mars.

2011 — NATO attack in Pakistan: NATO forces in Afghanistan attack a Pakistani check post in a friendly fire incident, killing 24 soldiers and wounding 13 others.
